Two models from the field

Source: vignettes/articles/field-models.Rmd
field-models.Rmd
library(multimod)

The toy model of the other articles fits on one screen. This article runs two models written by other people for real work: OSeMOSYS, which is read from its public source, and the energyRt reference model, which ships with multimod. Both are energy system models; neither was written with multimod in mind. Chunks that need a solver or the OSeMOSYS files run only where those are present; the numbers quoted in the text are from a run with everything installed.

OSeMOSYS

OSeMOSYS, the Open Source Energy Modelling System, is written in GNU MathProg. Its repository OSeMOSYS/OSeMOSYS_GNU_MathProg (Apache License 2.0, copyright 2010-2015 OSeMOSYS Forum steering committee) holds the model file src/osemosys.txt and the UTOPIA test case tests/utopia.txt. Nothing of it is bundled with multimod; this section reads a local clone whose path is in the environment variable MULTIMOD_OSEMOSYS_DIR. The reference result for UTOPIA is the objective glpsol reports on those two files, 29446.86.

Cite: Howells, M., Rogner, H., Strachan, N., Heaps, C., Huntington, H., Kypreos, S., Hughes, A., Silveira, S., DeCarolis, J., Bazilian, M. and Roehrl, A. (2011). OSeMOSYS: The Open Source Energy Modeling System. An introduction to its ethos, structure and development. Energy Policy, 39(10), 5850-5870. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enpol.2011.06.033

ose <- read_gmpl(file.path(osemosys_dir, "src", "osemosys.txt"),
                 file.path(osemosys_dir, "tests", "utopia.txt"))
ose

The reader returns 11 sets, 61 parameters, 68 variables and 95 equations. Twenty-six parameters carry UTOPIA data; six are formulas over other parameters (discount factors, the capital recovery factor, the annuity), and the rest take their declared defaults, among them a parametric default, DiscountRateIdv defaulting to DiscountRate[r].

validate(ose, stop_on_error = FALSE)$valid
as_gams(ose$parameters$CapitalRecoveryFactor$formula$expr)
cat(as_latex(ose$equations$CAa1_TotalNewCapacity$rhs))

JuMP

Formula parameters become Julia dictionaries computed from the data at run time, and the parametric default becomes a nested get():

# Each variable is declared over a full set product
@variable(model, RateOfDemand[REGION, TIMESLICE, FUEL, YEAR] >= 0)
@variable(model, Demand[REGION, TIMESLICE, FUEL, YEAR] >= 0)
@variable(model, StorageLevelYearStart[REGION, STORAGE, YEAR] >= 0)

@objective(model, Min, sum(TotalDiscountedCost[r, y] for r in REGION, y in YEAR))

optimize!(model)
println("Termination status: ", termination_status(model))
println("Objective value: ", objective_value(model))
ws <- tempfile("osemosys-")
dir.create(ws)
write_jump(ose, model_dir = ws)
data_jl <- readLines(file.path(ws, "solvers", "jump", "data.jl"))
cat(substr(grep("^CapitalRecoveryFactor = Dict", data_jl, value = TRUE), 1, 160), "...\n")
j <- solve_jump(ose, ws, verbose = FALSE)
j$objective
j$status

The objective matches glpsol’s 29446.86.

Solved in R, from the matrix

The same model goes through the matrix route without any generated code. OSeMOSYS declares every symbol over a set product with no domain mapping, restricts 34 of its 95 equations with data-dependent conditions, references lagged years (y-1, y+1) and defines six parameters by formula; the matrix backend expands the declared sets, evaluates the conditions, resolves the lags and computes the formulas itself.

h <- solve_highs(ose, attach = FALSE)
h$objective
nrow(build_row_index(ose))   # glpsol generates exactly this many rows

What does not work yet

Four storage-bracket equations (SC2_*, SC4_*) assemble with no coefficients on this case; UTOPIA’s storage is inactive, so the objective is unaffected, and model_to_lp() says so in a warning rather than hiding it. write_gams() output of this model is readable but not yet runnable without edits. There is no Pyomo reader.

energyRt

energyRt is an R package for energy system models that writes its own GAMS, MathProg, JuMP and Pyomo code. example_models$energyRt holds one of its reference scenarios, the “TOPIA” kit (seven regions, seasonal time slices, a base horizon), parsed by read_gams() from the GAMS template energyRt generates and populated with the scenario’s data.

str(example_models$energyRt$metadata)
#> List of 8
#>  $ source          : chr "energyRt TOPIA kit"
#>  $ scenario        : chr "R7 / topia_seasons / base horizon"
#>  $ repository      : chr "https://github.com/optimal2050/energyRt"
#>  $ license         : chr "Apache-2.0"
#>  $ energyRt_version: chr "0.90.0.9012"
#>  $ gams_source     : chr "gams/energyRt.gms"
#>  $ date_imported   : Date[1:1], format: "2026-10-04"
#>  $ note            : chr "Model structure parsed from energyRt's GAMS template with read_gams(include = FALSE); data attached from an int"| __truncated__

The dataset is derived from energyRt, Apache License 2.0, copyright the energyRt development team. The GAMS source is kept beside the parsed model:

gms <- example_models$energyRt$gams$model
length(gms)
#> [1] 3005
i <- grep("^eqTechCap", gms)[1]
cat(gms[i:(i + 4)], sep = "\n")
#> eqTechCap(tech, region, year)        Technology capacity
#> eqTechCapLo(tech, region, year)      Technology capacity lower bound
#> eqTechCapUp(tech, region, year)      Technology capacity upper bound
#> eqTechNewCapLo(tech, region, year)   Lower bound on new capacity
#> eqTechNewCapUp(tech, region, year)   Upper bound on new capacity
m <- example_models$energyRt$multimod
m
#> Model: 
#> Source:  C:/Users/admin/Documents/R/energyRt/gams/energyRt.gms 
#> Language:  GAMS 
#> Sets:  27 
#> Mappings:  324 
#> Aliases:  7 
#> Parameters:  218 
#> Variables:  93 
#> Equations:  153

The matrix route 

lp <- model_to_lp(m)
dim(lp$A)
#> [1] 19083 19218
r <- solve_highs(m, attach = FALSE)
r$objective
#> [1] 46398.42

Nineteen thousand rows and columns assemble and solve in a few seconds.

The file routes

The same model goes through each generated language; the objective is the one to compare.

ws <- tempfile("energyrt-")
dir.create(ws)
write_gmpl(m, model_dir = ws)
g <- solve_gmpl(m, ws, verbose = FALSE)
c(objective = g$objective, status = g$status)
#>          objective             status 
#> "46398.4234209741"          "OPTIMAL"
write_jump(m, model_dir = ws)
j <- solve_jump(m, ws, verbose = FALSE)
#> Loading solutions from: solvers/jump/solution
c(objective = j$objective, status = j$status)
#>          objective             status 
#> "46398.4234209742"          "OPTIMAL"

The generated Julia, one constraint:

jl <- readLines(file.path(ws, "solvers", "jump", "model.jl"))
i <- grep("@constraint", jl, fixed = TRUE)[1]
cat("```julia", jl[i:(i + 4)], "```", sep = "\n")
@constraint(
    model,
    eqTechSng2Sng[(h, r, c, cp, y, t) in meqTechSng2Sng],
    vTechOut[(h, cp, r, y, t)] == get(pTechCinp2use, (h, c, r, y, t), pTechCinp2useDef) * get(pTechUse2cact, (h, cp, r, y, t), pTechUse2cactDef) * get(pTechCact2cout, (h, cp, r, y, t), pTechCact2coutDef) * vTechInp[(h, c, r, y, t)]
)
write_pyomo(m, model_dir = ws, export_vars = TRUE)
p <- solve_pyomo(m, ws, solver = "highs", verbose = FALSE, load_results = TRUE)
c(objective = p$objective, status = p$status$termination)
#>          objective             status 
#> "46398.4234209742"          "optimal"

With everything installed the four routes return 46398.42; GLPK takes about ten seconds on this model, Pyomo and JuMP somewhat longer, mostly in start-up.

The GAMS source this model came from can also be regenerated:

out <- write_gams(m)
length(out)
#> [1] 2069

Any energyRt scenario enters the same way: energyRt’s multimod_from_energyRt() builds the model from an interpolated scenario, with the structure from the GAMS template and the data from the scenario’s tables.
